script: The shared administrative calendar. Payroll runs on fixed dates. A transaction has to be approved before its cutoff, and a time card has to be in by its deadline, or the pay waits for the next run. Vanderbilt publishes those dates in the H R Payroll Calendar.
People Experience publishes it on the Pay Calendar page of its site, under Payroll. There's one P D F for each year, with a page for each month. The 2026 and 2027 calendars are posted.

Find your pay group. Each row is one payroll: weekly, biweekly, monthly, academic monthly, or off cycle. For each, the calendar gives the pay period, the paycheck date, the H C M Transaction Cutoff, and when time cards are due.

Monthly pay. In 2026, the H C M Transaction Cutoff for monthly and academic monthly pay is the 18th, in every month but December, when it's the 16th. It stays the 18th even on a weekend, so finish on the last working day before it.
Weekly and biweekly pay. The cutoff is the Friday a week before payday, in nearly every pay period. Holiday weeks move it.
Time cards are due at noon on the Monday after the pay period ends. In holiday weeks the deadline moves, often to 10 a m, or to Tuesday. Monthly pay has no time card.
Off-cycle runs. The cutoff and the time card deadline are noon, two days before the paycheck date, usually a Wednesday.
Submit early enough for approvals. A transaction counts only once it's fully approved, so leave time for every approver to act before the cutoff, and track it with the notifications bell.
Miss the cutoff, and a change that arrives after payroll is calculated is picked up as a retroactive adjustment in a later run. The person may be paid late, or need a correction.
Two things to remember. Don't work from memory: dates move around holidays, and the December cutoff is early. And pending approvals don't pay.
